attempts.summary: On node1 (AlmaLinux 9), installed nginx serving HTTPS on port 8443 with a certificate signed by a locally-generated internal CA. A renewal script (/usr/local/sbin/renew-cert.sh) checks certificate expiry via `openssl x509 -checkend`, regenerates the cert when within 10 minutes of expiry, and reloads nginx (`systemctl reload nginx`) so the new cert is picked up without dropping in-flight connections. A systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, every 5 min, enabled at boot) drives this automatically. Opened firewalld port 8443/tcp permanently. Demonstrated the full renewal-and-hot-swap behavior by advancing the system clock into the renewal window while a continuous curl loop hit the service: renewal fired, the served certificate's serial changed, nginx reloaded, and all 70 requests during the operation returned HTTP 200 (zero downtime). Restored real time via chronyd and forced a fresh renewal so the live cert's validity window is correct. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol for node1: captured pre-reboot boot_id and service health, issued `systemctl reboot` with an ack that returned before disconnect, polled until reachable, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified nginx/cert-renew.timer/firewalld/chronyd all recovered with the HTTPS service still serving a CA-verifiable certificate.
